title: First-match search under predicate agreement
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $xs$ be a finite list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $p,q : \alpha \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ agree on every element of $xs$. Then the first element of $xs$ satisfying $p$, if any, is the same as the first element satisfying $q$; equivalently, the two searches return the same optional element.
replaced: Let $p$ and $q$ be Boolean predicates that agree on every element of a given list. Then the first element of the list satisfying $p$ equals the first element satisfying $q$.
